ruedas.what_es: Cada rueda es una malla tejida de alambre de acero con bandas de titanio. Es flexible, no se pincha y agarra bien el polvo lunar. Cada una tiene su propio motor.
ruedas.what_en: Each wheel is a woven mesh of steel wire with titanium treads. It is flexible, cannot go flat and grips lunar dust well. Each wheel has its own motor.

facts.value_es: 81,8 cm de diámetro y 23 cm de ancho
facts.value_en: 81.8 cm diameter, 23 cm wide

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: an 81.8 cm diameter, 23 cm wide tire made of zinc coated woven 0.083 cm diameter steel strands

facts.value_es: Las bandas de titanio cubren el 50 % de la zona de contacto
facts.value_en: Titanium chevrons cover 50% of the contact area

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: Titanium chevrons covered 50% of the contact area to provide traction.

facts.value_es: Se eligió la malla de alambre de General Motors frente a la rueda de aros de Bendix
facts.value_en: The General Motors wire mesh wheel was chosen over Bendix's hoop spring wheel

source.title: NASA NTRS: The Development of Wheels for the Lunar Roving Vehicle (NASA/TM-2009-215798)

facts.quote: in the end, the wire mesh wheel was chosen for the LRV

heritage.note_es: El neumático de resortes de NASA Glenn y Goodyear se inspiró en las ruedas de malla de alambre del LRV.
heritage.note_en: NASA Glenn and Goodyear's Spring Tire was inspired by the LRV wire-mesh wheels.

source.title: NASA NTRS: Design and Analysis of Shape Memory Spring Tires for Martian and Lunar Rover Vehicles

heritage.quote: Inspired by the flexible wire mesh tires used on three Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV) missions to the Moon on Apollo 15, 16, and 17

suspension.what_es: Cada rueda cuelga de una doble horquilla con barras de torsión que absorbe los golpes. Hay dirección adelante y atrás, así que el rover gira en espacios muy cerrados.
suspension.what_en: Each wheel hangs from a double wishbone with torsion bars that soaks up bumps. Steering works on both axles, so the rover can turn in very tight spaces.

facts.value_es: Doble horquilla horizontal con barras de torsión y amortiguador
facts.value_en: Double horizontal wishbone, upper and lower torsion bars, and a damper

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: The suspension consisted of a double horizontal wishbone with upper and lower torsion bars and a damper unit between the chassis and upper wishbone.

facts.value_es: Radio de giro de 3,1 m; se puede usar solo un eje
facts.value_en: Turning radius of 3.1 m; one axle can be used alone

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: giving a steering radius of 3.1 meters, or could be decoupled so only one set would be used for steering

facts.value_es: Unos 18 km/h (récord que se atribuye a Cernan, Apolo 17)
facts.value_en: About 18 km/h (record credited to Cernan, Apollo 17)

source.title: NASA Marshall Star, December 12, 2012 (PDF)

facts.quote: Cernan also holds the speed record of about 18 kilometers per hour.

bastidor.what_es: Es el esqueleto de aluminio, en tres partes unidas por bisagras. Se doblaba para caber en el costado del módulo lunar y se abría al bajarlo a la superficie.
bastidor.what_en: The aluminum skeleton, in three parts joined by hinges. It folded to fit on the side of the lunar module and unfolded as it was lowered to the surface.

facts.value_es: Tres partes con bisagra central, plegadas en el compartimento 1 del módulo lunar
facts.value_en: Three parts hinged in the center, folded into the Lunar Module quad 1 bay

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: hinged in the center so it could be folded up and hung in the Lunar Module quad 1 bay

facts.value_es: Aluminio 2219; 3,1 m de largo y 2,3 m entre ejes
facts.value_en: Aluminum alloy 2219; 3.1 m long with a 2.3 m wheelbase

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: The frame was 3.1 meters long with a wheelbase of 2.3 meters.

facts.value_es: 210 kg de masa; carga prevista de 490 kg
facts.value_en: 210 kg mass; 490 kg designed payload

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: The Lunar Roving Vehicle had a mass of 210 kg and was designed to hold a payload of an additional 490 kg

asientos.what_es: Dos asientos plegables lado a lado, de tubo de aluminio y correas de nailon. Cada uno tiene cinturón con velcro y reposapiés ajustable.
asientos.what_en: Two foldable side-by-side seats made of aluminum tube and nylon straps. Each has a Velcro seatbelt and adjustable footrests.

facts.value_es: Dos asientos plegables de tubo de aluminio con correas de nailon
facts.value_en: Two foldable seats of tubular aluminum with nylon webbing

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: two side-by-side foldable seats made of tubular aluminum with nylon webbing

facts.value_es: Cada asiento tiene reposapiés ajustable y cinturón de velcro
facts.value_en: Each seat has adjustable footrests and a Velcro seatbelt

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: each seat had adjustable footrests and a velcro seatbelt

facts.value_es: Se añadieron apoyos para los pies tras vuelos de gravedad reducida en el KC-135
facts.value_en: Toe holds were added after reduced-gravity KC-135 flights

source.title: NASA NTRS: The Lunar Roving Vehicle: Historical perspective (S. Morea, NASA MSFC, 1992)

facts.quote: Toe holds were incorporated as the result of early KC-135 flights simulating the 1/6-g environment of the Moon.

consola.what_es: Una palanca en T entre los asientos acelera, gira y frena las cuatro ruedas. Delante, la pantalla muestra velocidad, rumbo y energía, y el sistema de navegación indica el camino de vuelta al módulo.
consola.what_en: A T-shaped stick between the seats drives, steers and brakes. In front, the display shows speed, heading and power, and the navigation system points the way back to the lunar module.

facts.value_es: Palanca en T entre los asientos: cuatro motores de tracción, dos de dirección y frenos
facts.value_en: T-shaped hand controller between the seats: four drive motors, two steering motors and brakes

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: A T-shaped hand controller situated between the two seats controlled the four drive motors, two steering motors and brakes.

facts.value_es: Velocidad, rumbo, inclinación, energía y temperatura
facts.value_en: Speed, heading, pitch, power and temperature

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: gave information on the speed, heading, pitch, and power and temperature levels

facts.value_es: Giroscopio direccional y odómetro alimentan una computadora que calcula el regreso
facts.value_en: A directional gyro and odometer feed a computer that tracks the way back

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: Navigation was based on continuously recording direction and distance through use of a directional gyro and odometer

baterias.what_es: Dos baterías de plata y zinc, no recargables, dan la energía. Cada rueda tiene su propio motor eléctrico, así que el rover sigue andando si uno falla.
baterias.what_en: Two non-rechargeable silver-zinc batteries supply the power. Each wheel has its own electric motor, so the rover can keep going if one fails.

facts.value_es: Dos de 36 V, plata y zinc, no recargables, de 121 Ah
facts.value_en: Two 36 V silver-zinc, non-rechargeable, 121 amp-hr

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: two 36-volt silver-zinc potassium hydroxide non-rechargeable batteries with a capacity of 121 amp-hr

facts.value_es: Motor de 0,25 hp y 10 000 rpm con reductor armónico 80:1
facts.value_en: 0.25 hp motor, 10,000 rpm, with 80:1 harmonic drive

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: a DC series wound 0.25 hp motor capable of 10,000 rpm, attached to the wheel via an 80:1 harmonic drive

facts.value_es: Control térmico pasivo mantiene las baterías en su rango
facts.value_en: Passive thermal control keeps the batteries in range

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: Passive thermal controls kept the batteries within an optimal temperature range.

antena.what_es: Una antena de malla en forma de plato, al frente, apunta a la Tierra y lleva la señal de televisión. Una antena de voz en el centro permite hablar con Houston.
antena.what_en: A mesh dish antenna at the front points at Earth and carries the TV signal. A voice antenna on the center chassis allows talking with Houston.

facts.value_es: Montada en un mástil al frente, en el centro
facts.value_en: Mounted on a mast at the front center

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: A large mesh dish antenna was mounted on a mast on the front center of the rover.

facts.value_es: Envía la señal de televisión a la Tierra
facts.value_en: Beams the television signal to Earth

source.title: NASA NTRS: Development and Application of Color Television for Apollo XV and Beyond (S. Russell, RCA)

facts.quote: The high-gain antenna beamed the television signal to earth.

facts.value_es: Va en el chasis central
facts.value_en: Sits on the center chassis

source.title: NASA NTRS: The Lunar Roving Vehicle: Historical perspective (S. Morea, NASA MSFC, 1992)

facts.quote: the voice antenna on the center chassis

camara.what_es: Cámara a color montada al frente del rover. Desde Houston, un operador la movía y le cambiaba el zoom por radio, así el mundo veía la Luna casi en vivo.
camara.what_en: A color camera mounted at the front of the rover. In Houston an operator panned it and changed the zoom by radio, so the world watched the Moon almost live.

facts.value_es: Cámara de televisión a color, autónoma
facts.value_en: Self-contained color television camera

source.title: NASA NTRS: Development and Application of Color Television for Apollo XV and Beyond (S. Russell, RCA)

facts.quote: completely self-contained color camera unit

facts.value_es: Giro, inclinación, zoom y apertura se mandan desde Houston
facts.value_en: Pan, tilt, zoom and aperture commanded from Houston

source.title: NASA NTRS: Development and Application of Color Television for Apollo XV and Beyond (S. Russell, RCA)

facts.quote: Motorized drives in the lens assembly allow changes in the lens focal length and aperture.

facts.value_es: Pasaban 3,5 s entre pulsar un botón y ver el efecto
facts.value_en: 3.5 s passed between a button press and the visible response

source.title: NASA NTRS: Development and Application of Color Television for Apollo XV and Beyond (S. Russell, RCA)

facts.quote: When a pushbutton was pressed, 3.5 sec passed before any response was seen on the television screen.

herramientas.what_es: Atrás, una plataforma lleva las herramientas y los instrumentos científicos. También sirve para guardar las rocas y el suelo que los astronautas recogen.
herramientas.what_en: At the back, a platform carries the tools and science instruments. It also holds the rocks and soil the astronauts collect.

facts.value_es: El portaherramientas va atrás
facts.value_en: The tool carrier sits at the rear

source.title: NASA ALSJ: Apollo 16 onboard briefing, Lunar Roving Vehicle pages (PDF)

facts.quote: note the high gain antenna and the television camera in the front and the tool carrier in the rear

facts.value_es: Herramientas y equipo científico van sobre el chasis trasero
facts.value_en: Tools and science equipment ride on the aft chassis

source.title: NASA NTRS: The Lunar Roving Vehicle: Historical perspective (S. Morea, NASA MSFC, 1992)

facts.quote: scientific equipment and tools on the aft chassis

facts.value_es: 110,52 kg de muestras lunares
facts.value_en: 110.52 kg of lunar samples

source.title: NSSDCA: Apollo 17 Command and Service Module

facts.quote: collected 110.52 kg of lunar samples

guardabarros.what_es: Cubren cada rueda para frenar el polvo lunar que levanta. Son de fibra de vidrio. En el Apolo 17 se rompió uno y se arregló con mapas y cinta.
guardabarros.what_en: They cover each wheel to stop the lunar dust it kicks up. They are fiberglass. On Apollo 17 one broke and was fixed with maps and tape.

facts.value_es: Protectores de polvo sobre las ruedas
facts.value_en: Dust guards above the wheels

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

facts.quote: Dust guards were mounted above the wheels.

facts.value_es: Fibra de vidrio con resina epoxi
facts.value_en: Epoxy-impregnated fiberglass

source.title: Smithsonian NASM: Wheel, Lunar Rover (A19750830000)

facts.quote: Fender: Epoxy-impregnated fiberglass

facts.value_es: Cuatro de los 28 mapas lunares, cinta y dos pinzas
facts.value_en: Four of the 28 lunar maps, tape and two clamps

source.title: Smithsonian NASM: Duct Tape Auto Repair on the Moon

facts.quote: Their solution was to attach four of the 28 lunar maps with what Cernan would later call

missions.name: Apollo 15
missions.where_es: Hadley-Apeninos, región del mar de las Lluvias (Mare Imbrium), 26,1 N, 3,6 E
missions.where_en: Hadley-Apennine, Mare Imbrium region, 26.1 N, 3.6 E
missions.summary_es: David Scott y James Irwin estrenaron el rover en la Luna. Lo condujeron 27,8 km en 3 h 2 min. Llegaron a unos 5 km del módulo lunar, la mayor distancia hasta entonces.
missions.summary_en: David Scott and James Irwin were the first to use the rover on the Moon. They drove 27.8 km in 3 h 2 min and got about 5 km from the lunar module, a record at the time.

milestones.text_es: Primera conducción en la Luna: Scott prueba el rover tras desplegarlo.
milestones.text_en: First drive on the Moon: Scott test-drives the rover after deploying it.

source.title: NASA: 50 Years Ago: Apollo 15 on the Moon at Hadley-Apennine

milestones.quote: Scott took it for a brief test drive, becoming the first human to drive on the Moon.

milestones.text_es: Primera salida: el rover se descarga, se despliega y se conduce.
milestones.text_en: First moonwalk: the rover is unloaded, deployed and driven.

source.title: NSSDCA: Apollo 15 Lunar Module/ALSEP

milestones.quote: on 31 July from 13:13:10 UT to 19:45:59 UT, during which time the LRV was unloaded, deployed, and driven

milestones.text_es: Segunda salida: unos 5 km del módulo, lo más lejos que habían ido astronautas hasta entonces.
milestones.text_en: Second moonwalk: about 5 km from the module, farther than any astronauts had gone to that time.

source.title: NASA: 50 Years Ago: Apollo 15 on the Moon at Hadley-Apennine

milestones.quote: about 5 km from Falcon, the furthest any astronauts had traveled from their spacecraft up to that time

milestones.text_es: Total del rover: 27,8 km en 3 h 2 min; mayor alcance 5,0 km; tramo más largo 12,5 km.
milestones.text_en: Rover total: 27.8 km in 3 h 2 min; maximum range 5.0 km; longest traverse 12.5 km.

source.title: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

milestones.quote: the LRV was driven a total of 27.8 km in 3 hours, 2 minutes of driving time.

source.title: NSSDCA: Apollo 15 Command and Service Module

missions.name: Apollo 16
missions.where_es: Tierras altas de Descartes, 9,0 S, 15,5 E
missions.summary_es: John Young y Charles Duke recorrieron 26,7 km en 3 h 26 min. Probaron la velocidad del rover en su "Gran Premio". Un guardabarros se rompió, pero siguieron adelante.
missions.summary_en: John Young and Charles Duke drove 26.7 km in 3 h 26 min. They tested the rover's speed in their "Grand Prix". A fender tore off, but they carried on.

milestones.text_es: "Gran Premio": Young maneja el rover a toda marcha en la primera salida.
milestones.text_en: "Grand Prix": Young puts the rover through a speed run on the first moonwalk.

source.title: NASA: John Young Driving the Lunar Rover

milestones.quote: John W. Young in the "Grand Prix" run during the first Apollo 16 spacewalk at the Descartes landing site on April 21, 1972

milestones.text_es: Segunda salida: el traje de Young engancha y arranca el guardabarros trasero derecho.

milestones.quote: Young's suit caught on the right rear fender of the Rover, tearing it off

milestones.text_es: Tercera salida: viajan al cráter North Ray, 11,4 km de recorrido.
milestones.text_en: Third moonwalk: they travel to North Ray Crater, an 11.4 km traverse.

source.title: NSSDCA: Apollo 16 Lunar Module/ALSEP

milestones.quote: on the third, of 11.4 km, on 23 April from 15:25:28 UT to 21:05:31 UT they travelled to North Ray Crater

milestones.text_es: Total del rover: 26,7 km en 3 h 26 min; mayor alcance 4,5 km; tramo más largo 11,6 km.
milestones.text_en: Rover total: 26.7 km in 3 h 26 min; maximum range 4.5 km; longest traverse 11.6 km.

milestones.quote: the vehicle traversed 26.7 km in 3 hours 26 minutes of driving.

source.title: NSSDCA: Apollo 16 Command and Service Module

missions.summary_en: Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt drove 35.9 km in 4 h 26 min, the longest of the three missions. They got 7.6 km from the module. They fixed a fender with maps and tape.

milestones.text_en: First moonwalk: Cernan test-drives the rover around the lunar module.

milestones.text_en: Rover total: 35.9 km in 4 h 26 min; maximum range 7.6 km; longest traverse 20.1 km.

notes:
Verified 2026-11-22 by opening each page. ALSJ HTML pages (nasa.gov/history/alsj/...) redirected to the ALSJ landing page and the ALSJ Lunar Rover Operations Handbook PDFs returned 404 in this session, so the handbook and ALSJ transcripts were NOT used; the Apollo 16 onboard briefing PDF hosted by the ALSJ was readable and used. NTRS PDFs (tv, morea) are OCR text: quotes were chosen from clean passages and matched after whitespace normalisation by script.
DISTANCES: the data uses the NSSDC LRV page figures (A15 27.8 km, A16 26.7 km, A17 35.9 km). Disagreements: NSSDC mission pages give EVA totals of 27.9 km (A15), 27 km (A16, 'using the Lunar Roving Vehicle') and 30 km (A17); the NASA Marshall Star (2012) says Apollo 17 drove 21.7 miles (34.9 km) while Morea (NTRS) gives 17.3 mi (A15), 16.6 mi (A16) and 22.3 mi (A17).
TOP SPEED: NSSDC gives no top speed. NASA Marshall Star says Cernan 'holds the speed record of about 18 kilometers per hour'. Smithsonian says 'The LRV could reach speeds of up to 12 miles per hour' (https://airandspace.si.edu/collection-objects/lunar-roving-vehicle-4/nasm_A19750842000); NASA APOD says estimated top speed 8 mph (https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2001-june-9-apollo-17s-lunar-rover/). A search snippet said the ALSJ calls the 18 km/h figure an unverifiable claim, but that ALSJ page could not be opened, so treat that caveat as unverified. Present 18 km/h as a reported record, not a spec.
LOW-GAIN ANTENNA: not confirmed by any page I could quote, so it is not in the data. The antenna entry covers the high-gain mesh dish (NSSDC) and the 'voice antenna on the center chassis' (Morea). The mesh dish is described as a plate (what_*), not as an umbrella, because only a NASA APOD page says 'umbrella-shaped' (not used as a quoted fact).
DATES: milestone dates are UT calendar dates from the NSSDC Lunar Module pages. Apollo 17 EVA-1 ran 23:54 UT 11 Dec to 07:06 UT 12 Dec, so the fender knock-off is dated 1972-12-11 (EVA start); the map repair is dated 1972-12-12 (EVA-2 began 23:28 UT on 12 Dec and NASA says Cernan implemented the fix once on the surface); the A17 total is dated 1972-12-14 (EVA-3 ended 05:40 UT 14 Dec). Apollo 16 fender loss happened on EVA-2 (22 April) by the order of events in the NASA article, which does not print the date beside it. Apollo 15 first drive dated 1971-07-31 from the NSSDC EVA-1 entry. Apollo 16 Grand Prix dated 21 April from the NASA image article (some other sources place it on EVA-3; not used). Launch and splashdown dates are from the NSSDC CSM pages.
HERITAGE: only one verified entry (wheel -> Spring Tire; year 2023 is the NTRS record year). Camera, antennas, batteries, chassis, seats, console, tools and fenders: no NASA or Smithsonian page found that states later reuse, so left empty. Morea says the harmonic drive came from the shoe machinery business: that is prior art, not heritage, so not included.
SMALL ITEMS: 'Fenders are fiberglass' is from the Smithsonian wheel/fender object record. 'Tool carrier at rear' is from the Apollo 16 onboard briefing PDF. The Spanish name "Gran Premio" is a translation of the astronauts' nickname 'Grand Prix' (NASA Apollo 16 article). The Apollo 17 fender repair quote is cut at 'call' because the next word in the Smithsonian page has a broken character.
